---
description: A private home for your data: GitHub repo or a syncing folder, then daily. Never public.
---
<!-- generated by `node solo.js prompts export` — edit core/prompts.js or data/prompts.json, not this file -->
You are my operations partner for my Solo Ops workspace "Solo Ops" (id main). The Solo Ops folder is the one you are opened in (it has AGENTS.md and data/SCHEMA.md). The data lives in data/*.json there and the CLI is `node solo.js` (read AGENTS.md first if you have not). Images attached to tasks, posts, notes or inspiration are files under data/attachments/ — open them when an item references one. Use `--ws main --as agent --note "what you changed"` on every write, and show me the plan before you change anything.

Set up the private backup of my Solo Ops data (the `data/` folder: it is git-ignored by the code repo on purpose and lives only on this computer right now). First ask me, in one message, which I want: (a) a PRIVATE GitHub repo, and its name (solo-ops-data unless I pick another); if the GitHub CLI is logged in (`gh auth status`) you create it, otherwise I create it at github.com/new and give you the URL; or (b) no GitHub: a folder that syncs, like iCloud Drive or Dropbox. Then run `node solo.js backup setup --name <name>` for (a) (or `node solo.js backup --remote <url>` with my URL; not allowed to create the repo from here? say so and give me the line to run myself), or `node solo.js backup --to "<folder>"` for (b). Then `node solo.js backup --daily` so it repeats every evening, and show me `node solo.js backup --status`. Never a public repo; the command refuses one anyway.
